For an existing **upper-upscale hotel in North America**, I would begin with conversion-oriented collection brands, then compare them against more standardized full-service flags. Collection brands generally preserve more of the property’s identity and can reduce unnecessary redesign, although the actual PIP determines the economics.

## Primary collection-brand shortlist

| Brand | Best suited for | Owner considerations |
|---|---|---|
| **Autograph Collection – Marriott** | Distinctive urban hotels, resorts, historic properties and high-design independents | Usually one of the strongest candidates when the asset can support a differentiated story and premium ADR. Offers Marriott Bonvoy distribution, but admission and design expectations can produce a meaningful PIP. Marriott explicitly positions its collection brands for independent hotels and existing-hotel conversions. ([hotel-development.marriott.com](https://www.hotel-development.marriott.com/brands?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Curio Collection by Hilton** | Upper-upscale independent hotels and resorts with local character | Probably the closest Hilton equivalent to Autograph. Flexible enough to retain the hotel’s identity while accessing Hilton’s commercial platform and Hilton Honors; Hilton specifically identifies Curio as upper-upscale and conversion-friendly. ([stories.hilton.com](https://stories.hilton.com/releases/hiltons-curio-and-tapestry-collections-celebrate-200th-hotel-milestones?utm_source=openai)) |
| **The Unbound Collection by Hyatt** | Landmark, historic, resort or highly distinctive upper-upscale/luxury assets | Attractive where Hyatt has market “white space” or a strong corporate customer base. Hyatt positions Unbound specifically for upper-upscale and luxury independent properties. It is generally more selective than a conventional full-service conversion flag. ([hyatt.com](https://www.hyatt.com/development/ourbrands/theunboundcollectionbyhyatt?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Vignette Collection – IHG** | Independent luxury/lifestyle properties with an established identity | Worth considering for an asset positioned at the top of upper-upscale or capable of moving toward luxury. IHG identifies Vignette as a conversion-focused soft brand within its luxury and lifestyle portfolio. ([ihgplc.com](https://www.ihgplc.com/en/news-and-media/news-releases/2025/ihg-hotels-and-resorts-conversion-friendly-brands-fuel-growth-opportunities-for-owners?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Registry Collection Hotels – Wyndham** | Independent resorts, historic hotels and distinctive urban properties | A potentially attractive alternative where an owner wants upper-upscale positioning and Wyndham distribution without adopting a highly standardized hard brand. Wyndham identifies Registry as a soft brand in the upper-upscale segment. ([development.wyndhamhotels.com](https://development.wyndhamhotels.com/upscale-lifestyle-hotel-brands/?utm_source=openai)) |
| **MGallery Collection – Accor** | Design-led boutique, historic and lifestyle hotels | Accor positions MGallery in the upper-upscale collection segment and prioritizes conversions of existing buildings. It can be compelling in gateway, Canadian, resort or internationally oriented markets, although local Accor contribution should be tested carefully. ([group.accor.com](https://group.accor.com/en/news-stories/collection-brands-handwritten-emblems-mgallery?utm_source=openai)) |

## Additional flexible or lifestyle options

These should enter the screen when the asset’s positioning is somewhat below Autograph/Curio/Unbound or has a specific lifestyle profile:

- **Tribute Portfolio – Marriott:** Good for independent lifestyle hotels that fit Bonvoy but may not have the singular positioning expected of Autograph. Marriott has a defined conversion and PIP process for Tribute. ([hotel-development.marriott.com](https://www.hotel-development.marriott.com/resourcefiles/fdd-document/2023-tribute-portfolio-fdd-3-31-2023.pdf?utm_source=openai))
- **JdV by Hyatt:** Appropriate for smaller, neighborhood-oriented boutique hotels with active food-and-beverage or social spaces. Hyatt currently positions it as a full-service boutique collection. ([hyatt.com](https://www.hyatt.com/development/ourbrands?utm_source=openai))
- **Destination by Hyatt:** Particularly relevant for destination resorts, golf, ski, beach and experience-driven properties.
- **Hotel Indigo – IHG:** Strong candidate for locally inspired urban or resort lifestyle conversions, especially where the building or neighborhood provides a compelling design narrative. IHG has historically emphasized its flexible conversion approach. ([ihgplc.com](https://www.ihgplc.com/news-and-media/news-releases/2010/hotel-indigo-opens-second-property-in-nashville?utm_source=openai))
- **Kimpton – IHG:** Consider for a high-end lifestyle repositioning with substantial restaurant/bar potential and sufficient renovation capital.
- **Hyatt Centric:** Appropriate for lifestyle-oriented hotels in central urban or resort locations; Hyatt classifies the brand as upper-upscale, generally targeting roughly 100–250 rooms. ([hyatt.com](https://www.hyatt.com/development/ourbrands?utm_source=openai))
- **Graduate by Hilton:** A specialized but strong option for an upper-upscale asset in a major university market; Hilton describes Graduate as upper-upscale, bespoke and full-service. ([stories.hilton.com](https://stories.hilton.com/releases/hilton-launches-undergraduate-by-hilton?utm_source=openai))

## More standardized full-service conversion flags

If maintaining an independent identity is less important—or if the hotel needs clearer brand recognition—the owner should also solicit proposals from:

| Brand | Typical asset fit |
|---|---|
| **Delta Hotels by Marriott** | Corporate, airport, suburban and secondary-market full-service hotels; particularly relevant in Canada. Marriott has a formal conversion pathway, although the PIP and transition costs should be modeled carefully. ([hotel-development.marriott.com](https://www.hotel-development.marriott.com/resourcefiles/fdd-document/2022-delta-hotels-fdd.pdf?utm_source=openai)) |
| **DoubleTree by Hilton** | Broadest conventional conversion candidate for existing full-service hotels; works across urban, suburban, airport and resort locations. Hilton continues to identify DoubleTree as a major conversion engine. ([stories.hilton.com](https://stories.hilton.com/apac/releases/aravest-hilton-and-wee-hur-partner-to-debut-doubletree-by-hilton-singapore-robertson-quay-in-2026?utm_source=openai)) |
| **voco – IHG** | Flexible premium conversion for properties that can retain some individuality without becoming a full soft-brand hotel. IHG specifically identifies voco as conversion-friendly. ([ihgplc.com](https://www.ihgplc.com/en/news-and-media/news-releases/2025/ihg-hotels-and-resorts-conversion-friendly-brands-fuel-growth-opportunities-for-owners?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Crowne Plaza – IHG** | Business, meetings and airport hotels with substantial function space |
| **Hyatt Regency** | Larger full-service hotels, resorts and convention-oriented assets; Hyatt classifies it as upper-upscale and typically targets 200–2,000 rooms. ([hyatt.com](https://www.hyatt.com/development/ourbrands?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Wyndham Grand** | Upper-upscale resorts, conference hotels and full-service hotels in markets where Wyndham has useful distribution. ([development.wyndhamhotels.com](https://development.wyndhamhotels.com/upscale-lifestyle-hotel-brands/?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Renaissance, Sheraton or Marriott Hotels** | Potentially appropriate for larger institutional-quality assets, but generally more standardized and potentially more capital-intensive than a collection conversion |

## Recommended first-round brand process

For most assets, I would issue an initial request for brand proposal to **five or six candidates**:

1. **Autograph Collection**
2. **Curio Collection**
3. **The Unbound Collection**
4. **Vignette Collection or voco**
5. **Tribute Portfolio or DoubleTree**
6. **One market-specific alternative**—MGallery, Registry, Hyatt Centric, Destination, Graduate, Delta or Hyatt Regency

The decision should be based on a **10-year owner cash-flow comparison**, not simply the strongest consumer brand. Normalize each proposal for:

- Required PIP and renovation timing
- Key money or other brand support
- Base, incentive, royalty and program fees
- Loyalty-program reimbursement and redemption mix
- Central reservation and brand-channel contribution
- Expected ADR and occupancy lift
- Group, corporate-negotiated and international demand contribution
- Brand-mandated staffing and service levels
- F&B, lounge, spa and meeting-space requirements
- Territorial protection and nearby pipeline
- Franchise versus management structure
- Term, performance test, cure rights and exit/liquidated-damages provisions
- Ability to preserve the existing hotel name, design and local equity

**Practical conclusion:** For a distinctive asset, the most important initial comparison is usually **Autograph vs. Curio vs. Unbound**, with **Vignette, MGallery and Registry** as credible alternatives. For a more standardized corporate or meetings hotel, the screen should shift toward **Delta, DoubleTree, voco, Crowne Plaza and Hyatt Regency**.
